JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Jeanene, Layla, Mona, Pauline

payload.content:
Hi all — Pauline here. My top skill is mobile-development (0.61), and my availability is 8h. My costs are only reasonable on the ISSUE-0001 mobile-development tasks; my costs on ISSUE-0002 (ui-ux-design/testing) are prohibitive, so I will not claim those.

Plan: I intend to claim one ISSUE-0001 mobile-development task. My lowest-cost option is ISSUE-0001::triage, but I'm flexible on review/docs/test/implement if someone else needs triage more.

Could each of you state your intended claim so we avoid duplicates and cover the critical ISSUE-0002 tasks with whoever has the best skill match? I'd prefer we coordinate openly here to maximize the joint score.

Hi all — Mona here. Availability 7h, top skill testing (0.87). My costs strongly favor the critical ISSUE-0002 tasks: review=7.44, test=10.42, implement=15.89; my ISSUE-0001 costs are all 16–40, so I will NOT touch ISSUE-0001.

Intended claim: ISSUE-0002::review (critical, effort 4.0, my lowest cost 7.44, feasible within 7h). I can flex to ISSUE-0002::test (10.42) if someone else is a better fit for review — but review is my preference.

Please state your intended claims so we avoid duplicates. Also, whoever is strongest on the critical ISSUE-0002 implement (effort 8.0) should take it; I can't do it cheaply (15.89).

Hi all — Layla here. Availability 4.0h; top skills testing 0.90, mobile-development 0.77.

My private costs:
- ISSUE-0002::review=7.24 (effort 4.0, fits my 4h), test=11.74 (effort 5.6 > 4h, overloaded), implement=18.48 (effort 8.0, heavily overloaded)
- ISSUE-0001::triage=1.83, review=2.29, docs=2.29, test=3.21, implement=4.58

I can cover exactly one critical ISSUE-0002 task, and my best fit is review. Comparing the two ways Mona and I can split the critical review+test:
- Layla=review (7.24) + Mona=test (10.42) = 17.66
- Layla=test (11.74) + Mona=review (7.44) = 19.18

So the joint-cost-minimal split is Layla=review, Mona=test (saves 1.52). I'd like to claim ISSUE-0002::review. @Mona, would you flex to ISSUE-0002::test? If you strongly prefer review, I'll take test instead — either way we cover both critical tasks.

@Jeanene: please state your intent, especially for the critical ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 8.0) — that's the biggest lever and nobody has claimed it yet. I cannot do it (cost 18.48). @Pauline: your ISSUE-0001 mobile plan is fine by me; I'll stay off ISSUE-0001 unless critical tasks are covered.

Open to any better allocation. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Layla here — confirming. Mona and I are aligned: Layla = ISSUE-0002::review (cost 7.24), Mona = ISSUE-0002::test (cost 10.42). That covers 2 of the 3 critical tasks.

Remaining gap: ISSUE-0002::implement (critical, effort 8.0) is still unclaimed. @Jeanene — please state your intent ASAP. If implement fits your skills/availability, claim it; that's the single biggest lever (critical priority). If you can't, tell us and we'll accept the loss on that one rather than create infeasible/duplicate claims.

@Pauline: please take your best ISSUE-0001 mobile task (triage at 1.83 was your lowest) — nobody else will touch ISSUE-0001. That gives us 4 covered tasks total if Jeanene takes implement.

I'll hold my claim at ISSUE-0002::review unless someone has a strictly better joint-cost reallocation. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Pauline — confirming publicly: I will claim ISSUE-0001::triage (low, cost 2.25, my lowest). I stay off ISSUE-0002. @Jeanene: the only unclaimed critical task is ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 8.0) — please claim it if feasible, otherwise say so explicitly. Layla=review, Mona=test as agreed.
Pauline — FINAL LOCK: ISSUE-0001::triage. (Layla=ISSUE-0002::review, Mona=ISSUE-0002::test, Jeanene=ISSUE-0002::implement if feasible.) No duplicates from me.

Mona — FINAL LOCK (planning, iter=1): Mona = ISSUE-0002::test (critical, effort 5.6 <= my 7h availability, no overload, cost 10.42). Verified jointly better than the reversed split (Layla=review 7.24 + Mona=test 10.42 = 17.66 < Mona=review 7.44 + Layla=test 11.74 = 19.18), so this is a transparent joint-cost minimization, not a side deal.

Summary of agreed allocation (all stated openly here):
- Pauline = ISSUE-0001::triage (low)
- Layla = ISSUE-0002::review (critical)
- Mona = ISSUE-0002::test (critical)
- Jeanene = ISSUE-0002::implement (critical, effort 8.0) — still UNCLAIMED and unstated.

@Jeanene: this is your last call. If implement fits your skills/availability, claim it; it's the biggest lever (critical). If it does not fit, please say so explicitly so we don't end with a duplicate/infeasible claim. If it goes unfilled, note the environment may randomly fill it — better to state your intent clearly.

I will commit Mona = ISSUE-0002::test in the execution phase unless a strictly better joint reallocation is proposed before then.

Layla — final planning lock (iter=1). I will claim ISSUE-0002::review (critical, effort 4.0 = my availability, cost 7.24, feasible, no overload). This is my lowest-cost critical option and the joint-cost-minimal split with Mona=test (17.66 vs 19.18 reversed).

Agreed allocation:
- Layla = ISSUE-0002::review (critical)
- Mona = ISSUE-0002::test (critical)
- Pauline = ISSUE-0001::triage (low)
- Jeanene = ISSUE-0002::implement (critical) — still unstated; please state intent.

I will commit Layla = ISSUE-0002::review in execution unless a strictly better joint reallocation appears.
